item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
780
ABPZ20 KNHC 261722
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sat Sep 26 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located a few hundred miles west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes,
Mexico, on Hurricane Odalys, located well west-southwest of the
southern tip of Baja California, and on Hurricane Nolo, located
south of the Big Island of Hawaii.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec (EP90):
Showers and thunderstorms continue to develop in association with an
area of low pressure south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Additional
development of the system is anticipated due to conducive
environmental conditions and a tropical depression is expected to
form in the next day or so. This system is forecast to continue
moving slowly to the west-northwest or northwest, staying parallel
to the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure is expected to form within the next day
or two about 1000 miles to the east-southeast of the Hawaiian
Islands. Environmental conditions are expected to be conducive for
development of the system, and a tropical depression is likely to
form during the early to middle part of next week. The system is
should move generally northeastward, and remain well east-southeast
of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Papin

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.8N 123.7W
ABOUT 910 MI...1470 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA

PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 360 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...965 MB...28.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Odalys was located 
near latitude 19.8 North, longitude 123.7 West. Odalys is moving 
toward the north near 7 mph (11 km/h), and this motion is expected 
to continue through today, followed by a sharp turn toward the east 
and then south-southeast by early next. 
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 105 mph (165 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Rapid weakening is forecast over the next 
several days, and Odalys is anticipated to become a post-tropical 
cyclone by early next week. 
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 965 mb (28.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Hurricane Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 261446
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Odalys Discussion Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
800 AM PDT Sat Sep 26 2026

The structure of Odalys this morning appears to be quickly going 
downhill. The small eye that had been associated with the hurricane 
is no longer seen on geostationary satellite imagery. An earlier 
AMSR3 microwave pass also showed the inner core has degraded as 
southerly vertical wind shear quickly increases, now diagnosed at 32 
kt by UW-CIMSS. Both subjective and objective satellite intensity 
estimates are decreasing, and the initial intensity has been lowered 
to 90 kt for this advisory. 

With the abrupt increase in shear, Odalys is likely to continue 
rapidly weakening in the short-term. Most of the model guidance 
shows the vertical structure decoupling in the next 24-36 h as shear 
imports nearby dry air is into the circulation's core. The NHC 
intensity forecast was lowered quite a bit form the previous one, 
partially due to the lower initial intensity, but also with the 
expectation the small tropical cyclone will quickly succumb to the 
unfavorable environment. The latest forecast now shows Odalys 
becoming a remnant low in 48 h and dissipating by the mid portion of 
next week. 

The hurricane continues to move northward, with an estimated motion 
at 360 degree at 6 kt. A deep-layer trough to its northwest should 
maintain this general steering for the next 12-24 h, though as the 
the system decouples and becomes vertically shallow it should turn 
sharply back to the southeast or even south as it becomes more 
influenced by broad low-level ridging to its northwest. The latest 
NHC track is shifted slightly north in the short-term, but was also 
shifted westward after Odalys become a remnant low, following the 
latest trends in the HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA) and 
Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI) guidance.
 
Distant moisture from Hurricane Odalys and Polo will be transported
into the southwestern United States this weekend and early next
week, and may indirectly contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash
flood threat in the region. See products issued by the Weather
Prediction Center for more information.

item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM MST Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 261738
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Intermediate Advisory Number 24A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
1100 AM MST Sat Sep 26 2026
 
...POLO STILL A POWERFUL CATEGORY 4 HURRICANE...
...FORECAST TO MAKE LANDFALL IN BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR ON MONDAY AS
A STRONG HURRICANE... 
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM MST...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.3N 111.2W
ABOUT 330 MI...530 KM SSW OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
ABOUT 455 MI...730 KM S OF CABO SAN LAZARO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...145 MPH...230 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...936 MB...27.64 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* Punta Eugenia to Santa Fe
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area.  A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.
 
Watches will likely be required for the east coast of the Baja
California Peninsula later today.  Interests in portions of
northwestern mainland Mexico should monitor the progress of Polo.
Watches may be required for that area tonight or early Sunday.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM MST (1800 UTC), the center of Hurricane Polo was located 
near latitude 18.3 North, longitude 111.2 West. Polo is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A turn toward the 
northwest is expected this afternoon, followed by a northward motion 
on Sunday. By Monday, Polo is expected to turn northeastward and 
approach Baja California Sur.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 145 mph (230 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Polo is a category 4 hurricane on the 
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. Gradual weakening is forecast 
during the next couple of days, however Polo is expected to be a 
strong hurricane when it approaches Baja California Sur on Monday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125
miles (205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 936 mb (27.64 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are possible within the watch area by
Monday afternoon, with tropical storm conditions possible in the
southern portion of the watch area by Sunday night into early
Monday. These conditions are expected to spread northward during the
day on Monday.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8
inches with maximum amounts of 10 inches across portions of Baja
California Sur. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding
and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURGE: A storm surge could produce significant coastal flooding in
areas of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be
accompanied by large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will continue affecting the coast of
southwestern Mexico during the next day or two. Swells will also
spread northward along the coast of west-central Mexico and the Baja
California Peninsula through the weekend. These swells are likely
to cause life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding.
Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 24
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 261451
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 AM MST Sat Sep 26 2026
 
Infrared satellite imagery shows that the eye of Polo has become 
cloud filled since the previous advisory.  This appears to be a 
result of an increase in shear over the system.  The subjective 
Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB was unchanged from earlier, 
however objective estimates have decreased and range from about 
125-142 kt.  Therefore, the initial intensity for this advisory has 
been reduced to 135 kt, which could be slightly generous.

Some fluctuations in intensity are still possible today, however 
with the gradually increasing shear, slow weakening seems to be the 
more likely scenario during the next 24 to 48 hours.  After that 
time, a more significant increase in southwesterly shear is expected 
which is likely to cause an additional decrease in wind speed as 
Polo approaches the Baja Peninsula.  The latest NHC intensity 
forecast is a blend of the typically reliable HFIP corrected 
consensus and Google Deep Mind aids.  Regardless of the exact 
intensity forecast, Polo is expected to be a strong hurricane when 
it reaches Baja California Sur.
 
The initial motion estimate is west-northwestward, or 295 degrees at 
9 kt.  There is once again no significant change to the track 
forecast reasoning.  Polo is expected to turn northwestward later 
today, and then northward on Sunday as it moves around the western 
periphery of a mid-level ridge over Mexico. By Monday, a mid-level 
trough approaching the west coast of the United States should cause 
Polo to turn northeastward.  This motion is expected to take the 
cyclone over the Baja Peninsula and into northwestern Mexico late 
Monday through Tuesday.  While the track guidance is in generally 
good agreement on the overall scenario, there are some large 
difference in the forward speed of Polo after the northeastward 
turn, which results in a large spread as to when the storm reaches 
the Baja Peninsula. The NHC forecast is along the faster side of the 
guidance with the typically better performing HFIP corrected 
consensus aid and the Google Deep Mind ensemble mean. 
  
Distant moisture from Hurricane Polo and Odalys will be transported
into the southwestern United States this weekend and early next
week, and may indirectly contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash
flood threat in the region. See products issued by the Weather
Prediction Center for more information.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Polo is forecast to approach the west coast of the Baja
California peninsula on Monday as a hurricane, and a Hurricane
Watch is in effect for that region. Tropical storm conditions
could reach portions of the coast as soon as Sunday night or early 
Monday, making further preparations difficult. A storm surge will 
be possible, especially in areas of onshore winds.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo may begin to impact Baja 
California Sur late Sunday into Monday. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.
 
3. Dangerous surf and rip currents are likely along portions of
the northwest coast of Mexico and Baja California for the next
several days.
